title: How the son came to Havana and was kept from society clubs
summary: He explains the son came from Oriente, spread after soldiers learned the tres in Santiago, and was barred from society clubs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Okay, at that time, Did you know or hear of anything about - ah - the son?
El son come from Oriente, you know close to Guantanamo, whatever, Oriente.
Was it popular then? When you were growing up?

We don't know about it; there was a war, a civil war like - created by Maximo Gomez, in Santiago de Cuba, that became black fighting against white. Evaristo Tenor and few veterans from the liberation army and he create that in order - - -
Who created?
Maximo Gomez, I mean, Jose Miguel Gomez.
Was he white Cuban or black Cuban?
He was a - he was a half-breed.
I see. And what was his reason for creating this friction between whites and blacks?
In order to - to to disturb the political campaign to ah - you know, to create panic.
Was he running for office?
Yes, he was running. He wanted to be elected.
So he needed a cause to get reelected.
Absolutely.
So, tell me what happened.

So, when that thing started in Santiago de Cuba, he sent the regular army from Havana to Santiago de Cuba to stop the revolution, and Godines, that was the first tres player, the guitar player with Sexteto Habanero, and few other guys - they was so rhythmical - the economy was very bad in those days - so they went out there and they learned how to play the tres in Santiago de Cuba.
I see. The soldiers from Havana went there and they learned how to play .........
And they brought that to Havana.
The rhythm is son.
The son ....
Oh, I see.

The son. Now, now, when they brought that, on account that was black, they - was played among blacks, that type of music, like here, jazz among the new - among blacks - so they was good, you know, the people start to like because they were very rhythmic and very, very acceptable music; so in those days no club, no incorporated club will allow to play son in the - in the society.
It was banned?
- - - between the black - - - club they don't allow the sexteto to play; they were dancing the charanga or tipica - the one with bombardino and and figle and trumpet.
